rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib derives warūd from going to water, then notes its broader use.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الورود أصله قصد الماء ثم يستعمل في غيره

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes sending a bucket down from drawing it up; an unnamed view reverses the verbs.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الورود أصله قصد الماء ثم يستعمل في غيره. انتهى، وقال دلوت الدلو إذا أرسلتها، وأدليتها إذا أخرجتها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says concealment is the opposite of making something public.
rows.anchor: وقال الإسرار خلاف الإعلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the boy is separated from the bucket-drawing to mark the unexpected outcome: they expected water, not a child.
rows.anchor: إيراده بالفصل مع أنه متفرع وقوعا على إدلاء الدلو للدلالة على أنه كان أمرا غير مترقب الوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling out “good news” treats an abstract emotion like grief or woe as present, making its arrival vivid.
rows.anchor: ونداء البشرى كنداء الأسف والويل ونظائرهما للدلالة على حضوره وجلاء ظهوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God knows what they do” can condemn the caravan's conduct and warn that they will answer for it.
rows.anchor: مفاده ذم عملهم والإبانة عن كونه معصية محفوظة عليهم سيؤاخذون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God's foreknowledge directed Yusuf's removal from the well and sale so he could attain the kingship and honor already decreed for him.
rows.anchor: ذلك إنما كان بعلم من الله أراد بذلك أن يبلغ يوسف مبلغه الذي قدر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passing caravan sent a water-drawer into the well; Yusuf emerged holding the rope, was concealed as merchandise, and God knew or ordained the course of events.
rows.anchor: فأرسلوا من يطلب لهم الماء فأرسل دلوه في الجب ثم لما أخرجها فاجأهم بقوله يا بشرى هذا غلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A paltry price is below the item's fair value.
rows.anchor: الثمن البخس هو الناقص عن حق القيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counted dirhams are few; large sums were weighed rather than counted.
rows.anchor: ودراهم معدودة أي قليلة والوجه فيه - على ما قيل - أنهم كانوا إذا كثرت الدراهم أو الدنانير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dirhams were the silver currency then in circulation; sharaahu means selling, while zuhd can mean aversion or wariness.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالدراهم النقود الفضية الدائرة بينهم يومئذ، والشراء هو البيع، والزهد هو الرغبة عن الشيء أو هو كناية عن الاتقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronouns refer to the caravan: it sold Yusuf cheaply and hid his identity for fear he would be reclaimed.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من السياق أن ضميري الجمع في قوله { وشروه } { وكانوا } للسيارة

rows.speaker: معظم المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators take both pronouns to mean Yusuf's brothers, who claimed he was their slave after he fell into the well and sold him to the caravan.
rows.anchor: ومعظم المفسرين على أن الضميرين لإخوة يوسف والمعنى أنهم باعوا يوسف من السيارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the alternative reading, the brothers sold Yusuf for a low price and the caravan appeared disinterested.
rows.anchor: أن الإخوة باعوه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانت السيارة من الراغبين عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one explanation, the caravan feigned disinterest so the price would not rise.
rows.anchor: وكانت السيارة من الراغبين عنه يظهرون من أنفسهم الزهد والرغبة لئلا يعلو قيمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the caravan truly avoided buying Yusuf because the affair seemed suspicious and he lacked the appearance of a slave.
rows.anchor: أو يرغبون عن اشترائه حقيقة لما يحدسون أن الأمر لا يخلو من مكر وأن الغلام ليس فيه سيماء العبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that the brothers had not been explicitly mentioned again as an antecedent for these pronouns.
rows.anchor: ولم يقع للإخوة بعد ذلك ذكر صريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading assigns the first pronoun to the brothers and the second to the caravan, which supposedly feigned disinterest to hold down the price or truly avoided a suspicious purchase.
rows.anchor: أو أن أول الضميرين للإخوة والثانى للسيارة والمعنى أن الإخوة باعوه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانت السيارة من الراغبين عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative pronoun readings lack contextual support: the previous plural refers to the caravan, the brothers have not been reintroduced, and the next verse presents the Egyptian purchase as the completed sale.
rows.anchor: وسياق الآيات لا يساعد على شيء من الوجهين فضمائر الجمع في الآية السابقة للسيارة ولم يقع للإخوة بعد ذلك ذكر صريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Narrations say the brothers appeared at the well, claimed Yusuf as their slave, and sold him cheaply; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes the contextual readings do not dispose of these reports.
rows.anchor: أن إخوة يوسف حضروا هناك وأخذوا يوسف منهم بدعوى أنه عبدهم سقط في البئر ثم باعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed sense of sharaahu as “they bought him” is attested in Arabic but is ruled out here by context.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن الشراء في الآية بمعنى الاشتراء وهو مسموع وهو نظير الاحتمالين السابقين مدفوع بالسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan took Yusuf to Egypt, where a local buyer purchased him and brought him into his household.
rows.anchor: السياق يدل على أن السيارة حملوا يوسف معهم إلى مصر وعرضوه هناك للبيع فاشتراه بعض أهل مصر وأدخله في بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's refined traits were not new at maturity; their roots and signs were already present in childhood.
rows.anchor: وهذه صفات لا تنمو في الإنسان إلا وأعراقها ناجمة فيه أيام صباوته وآثارها لائحة من سيماه من بادئ أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz wanted Yusuf raised in his private household as one of his closest people, able to assist his important aims.
rows.anchor: حتى تمنى أن ينشأ يوسف عنده في خاصة بيته فيكون من أخص الناس به ينتفع به في أموره الهامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adoption could make Yusuf an heir to the Aziz's household.
rows.anchor: أو يدخل في أرومته ويكون ولدا له ولامرأته بالتبنى فيعود وارثا لبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's striking beauty and excellent character were already visible in childhood; his patience, dignity, refinement, wisdom, and noble origin explain the Aziz's interest.
rows.anchor: كان ذا جمال بديع يبهر العقول ويوله الألباب، وكان قد أوتى مع جمال الخلق حسن الخلق صبورا وقورا لطيف الحركات مليح اللهجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz seems to have been infertile, since he and his wife hoped to adopt Yusuf as their son.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يمكن أن يستظهر أن العزيز كان عقيما لا ولد له من زوجته ولذلك ترجى أن يتبنى هو وزوجته يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz is the buyer and his wife is the Azizah; honoring Yusuf's stay means personally caring for him and giving him a dignified place.
rows.anchor: فقوله { وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر } أي العزيز { لامرأته } وهى العزيزة { أكرمي مثواه } أي تصدي بنفسك أمره واجعلي له مقاما كريما عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz anticipates Yusuf's help in important aims or adoption as a son, who would inherit the household.
rows.anchor: { عسى أن ينفعنا } في مقاصدنا العالية وأمورنا الهامة { أو نتخذه ولدا } بالتبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two mentions of Yusuf's establishment express the same divine care: one follows the pit and sale, the other his release from prison and authority over Egypt.
rows.anchor: والعناية في الموضعين واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If establishment means his comfortable placement in the Aziz's house, the comparison to that event is a rhetorical self-simile that highlights its abundant qualities, not a defective tautology.
rows.anchor: فالتشبيه من قبيل تشبيه الشيء بنفسه ليدل به على غزارة الأوصاف المذكورة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes this rhetorical comparison from a defective self-simile, illustrated by the cited line about people sitting surrounded by water.
rows.anchor: وليس من القسم المذموم من تشبيه الشيء بنفسه كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic examples that follow present God's way of leading disbelievers astray and striking parables as recurring patterns modeled by an instance.
rows.anchor: كذلك يضل الله الكافرين غافر 74 وقوله كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال الرعد 17

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: In Abu Hamza's report, Ali ibn al-Husayn orders that no Friday petitioner leave without food.
rows.anchor: لا يعبر على بابى سائل إلا أطعمتموه فإن اليوم يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: He explains that an apparently undeserving petitioner could still be truly entitled, and refusing such a person risks the calamity that befell Jacob's household.
rows.anchor: أخاف أن يكون بعض من يسألنا محقا فلا نطعمه ونرده فينزل بنا أهل البيت ما نزل بيعقوب وآله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that We teach him” states one purpose of Yusuf's establishment, attached to an omitted purpose phrase because further aims cannot fit the present discussion; 6:75 is a parallel construction.
rows.anchor: بيان لغاية التمكين المذكور واللام للغاية، وهو معطوف على مقدر والتقدير مكنا له في الأرض لنفعل به كذا وكذا ولنعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prevails over every affair in creation: each created cause is subject to His will and cannot escape or precede Him; people err when they treat visible causes as independent agents.
rows.anchor: كل شأن من شؤن الصنع والإيجاد من أمره تعالى وهو تعالى غالب عليه وهو مغلوب له مقهور دونه

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: As narrated by Abu Hamza al-Thumali, Ali ibn al-Husayn says he ordered food for every Friday petitioner, fearing that turning away a deserving person would bring Jacob's family's calamity; Jacob's family once ignored a hungry, fasting stranger despite their customary charity.
rows.anchor: في المعاني بإسناده عن أبي حمزة الثمالي قال صليت مع علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام الفجر بالمدينة يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: In Abu Hamza's report, Jacob's sons planned to kill Yusuf, but their eldest persuaded them to cast him into a well; they later lied that a wolf ate him, and Jacob grieved yet trusted the truthful dream God had shown him.
rows.anchor: فقال كبيرهم { لا تقتلوا يوسف } ولكن { ألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين }

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: The next morning, the brothers found a caravan drawing water; the water-drawer pulled Yusuf up, and he announced that a boy had been found.
rows.anchor: فلما انتهوا إلى الجب وجدوا بحضرة الجب سيارة وقد أرسلوا واردهم فأدلى دلوه فإذا جذب دلوه فإذا هو غلام

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: The brothers claimed Yusuf as their slave, threatened to kill him unless he agreed, and sold him to a caravan member for twenty dirhams; the buyer took him to Egypt and sold him to its king.
rows.anchor: فاشتراه رجل منهم بعشرين درهما وكان إخوته فيه من الزاهدين وسار به الذي اشتراه من البدو حتى أدخله مصر

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Yusuf was nine when placed in the well, and Jacob's home was a twelve-day journey from Egypt.
rows.anchor: فقلت كم كان بين منزل يعقوب يومئذ وبين مصر فقال مسيرة اثنا عشر يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report has a continuation elsewhere; some of its details may seem unlike the verses' apparent sense, but reflection resolves the difficulty.
rows.anchor: وللحديث ذيل سنورده في البحث الروائي التالى إن شاء الله تعالى وفيه نكات ربما لم تلائم ظاهر ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This episode covers Yusuf's years in the Aziz's house, the Aziz's wife and city women pursuing him, and the remarkable chastity and devotion to God he displayed through these trials.
rows.anchor: تتضمن الآيات قصته عليه السلام أيام لبثه في بيت العزيز وقد ابتلي فيها بحب امرأة العزيز له ومراودتها اياه عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bulūgh al-ashudd begins at about eighteen, when youthful bodily strength is established; here it means the start of youth, not its middle or age forty.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد به الانتهاء إلى أول سن الشباب دون التوسط فيه أو الانتهاء إلى آخره كالأربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the reported ages thirty and thirty-three for reaching maturity.
rows.anchor: فلا مجال لما ذكره بعضهم إن المراد ببلوغ الأشد بلوغ الثلاثين أو الثلاث والثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥukm is decisive judgment that removes doubt in disputed matters; for Yusuf it encompasses sound insight into theology, ethics, law, and social conduct.
rows.anchor: الحكم هو القول الفصل وإزالة الشك والريب من الأمور القابلة للاختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's divinely given judgment is God's own judgment, as his words in prison show; this is the kind of judgment Abraham sought from God.
rows.anchor: يعلم أن هذا الحكم الذي أوتيه كان هو حكم الله فكان حكمه حكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge given by God is free from ignorance, just as divine judgment given to Yusuf is free from whim and demonic suggestion; God's command is always fulfilled.
rows.anchor: علم لا يخالطه جهل كما أن الحكم المذكور معه حكم لا يخالطه هوى نفساني ولا تسويل شيطاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These gifts are not arbitrary: good and corrupt souls bear different fruit, so “this is how We reward the good” makes Yusuf's judgment and knowledge a reward for excellence.
rows.anchor: حيث يدل على أن هذا الحكم والعلم اللذين آتاهما الله إياه لم يكونا موهبتين ابتدائيتين لا مستدعى لهما أصلا بل هما من قبيل الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward principle may extend to every kind of good deed, with wisdom and knowledge suited to the person's excellence; divine light is also promised to believers.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى يجزي كل محسن على اختلاف صفات الإحسان - شيئا من الحكم والعلم يناسب موقعه في الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example of one who was spiritually dead but received life and a light to walk among people illustrates God's gift to the good.
rows.anchor: أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib derives murāwada from gently and repeatedly seeking something; it is trying to turn another person toward one's own desire.
rows.anchor: قال في المفردات الرود هو التردد في طلب الشيء برفق ومنه الرائد لطالب الكلاء

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān defines murāwada as gently requesting an action, from seeking pasture; the term is not used for demanding a debt.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع المراودة المطالبة بأمر بالرفق واللين ليعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form in “she locked the doors” can indicate repeated shutting or emphasize how firmly the doors were secured.
rows.anchor: وإنما شدد ذلك لتكثير الإغلاق أو للمبالغة في الإيثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haita lak is a beckoning expression, while maʿādh Allāh is an absolute-object verbal noun standing in place of its verb, “I seek refuge in God.”
rows.anchor: وهيت لك اسم فعل بمعنى علم، ومعاذ الله أي أعوذ بالله معاذا فهو مفعول مطلق قائم مقام فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although concise, the verse signals the outline of the seduction episode; its circumstances can be recovered from its wording, context, and other clues in the story.
rows.anchor: على ما فيها من الإيجاز تنبئ عن إجمال قصة المراودة غير أن التدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge given to Yusuf includes the interpretation of events and dreams promised earlier and later described by him as taught by his Lord.
rows.anchor: وهذا العلم المذكور في الآية يتضمن ما وعد الله سبحانه تعليمه ليوسف من تأويل الأحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf entered the Aziz's house as a silent child slave; no one asked his lineage, and it became known only years later when he identified his fathers in prison.
rows.anchor: فليس للعبيد بيوت ولم يكن من المعهود أن يحفظ للأرقاء أنساب وهو ساكت مختوم على لسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He remembered Jacob's teaching about monotheism, his prophetic dream, and God's assurance in the well that divine care would later let him tell his brothers what they had done.
rows.anchor: فهو على ذكر مما بثه إليه أبوه يعقوب النبي من حقيقة التوحيد ومعنى العبودية ثم ما بشر به من الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trust in God's hidden care softened Yusuf's repeated ordeals; he endured without complaint or despair and later said God does not waste the reward of the pious and patient.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الذي هون عليه ما نزل به من النوائب، وتواتر عليه من المحن والبلايا فصبر عليها على ما بها من المرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's love of God increasingly occupied his inner life; his words about refuge, monotheism, God's judgment, and divine guardianship reveal this devotion.
rows.anchor: وهذا بمكان من الوضوح لمن تدبر فيما تحكي عنه السورة من المحاورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf was wholly absorbed in divinely bestowed love, which made him forget himself and everything else; God had purified him for Himself alone.
rows.anchor: فقد كان شبحا ما وراءه إلا محبة إلهية أنسته نفسه وشغلته عن كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Yusuf first appeared merely a young Hebrew slave, the Aziz's order to honor him reveals that he discerned dignity and promise in the boy.
rows.anchor: يكشف أنه شاهد منه وقارا وتمكينا وتفرس فيه عظمة وكبرياء نفسانية أطمعته في أن ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz's wife treated Yusuf like a treasured jewel rather than an ordinary slave and increasingly loved his exceptional beauty and perfection.
rows.anchor: لا كما يهتم في أمر رقيق مملوك بل كما يعنى بأمر جوهر كريم أو قطعة كبد وتحبه لبديع جماله وغزير كماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Yusuf reached puberty, the Azizah could no longer restrain her love despite her rank, prestige, and customary modesty.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا بلغ الحلم واستوى على مستوى الرجال لم تملك نفسها دون أن تعشقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She considered herself Yusuf's mistress and him her slave, apparently entitled to his obedience.
rows.anchor: وكانت فيما تزعم سيدة يوسف وهو عبدها المملوك لا يسعه إلا أن يطيعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Azizah repeatedly hoped for Yusuf's intimacy, used charm and flirtation, and may have mistaken his patience and silence for encouragement before finally isolating him behind locked doors.
rows.anchor: ولعل الذي كانت تشاهده من صبر يوسف وسكوته كان يغرها فيما ترومه ويغريها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Azizah seated the women, served fruit, gave each a knife, and then summoned the previously concealed Yusuf; seeing him, they cut their hands instead of the fruit.
rows.anchor: آتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا وقد هيأت لهن وقدمت إليهن الفاكهة، عند ذلك أمرت يوسف أن يخرج إليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extreme love or fright can overwhelm attention and bodily control, causing a person to act incoherently or do the opposite of what was intended.
rows.anchor: فإن نفس الإنسان إذا انجذبت إلى شيء مما تفرط في حبه أو تخافه وتهوله اضطربت وبهتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Azizah's passion accumulated gradually, whereas the city women were struck suddenly by Yusuf's beauty, lost judgment, and exposed their desire.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا هو الفرق بين العزيزة وبينهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the formal household, their rank, marriages, seclusion, and recent criticism of the Azizah, the women abandoned decorum when Yusuf appeared before them.
rows.anchor: وهن في بيت العزيز وهو بيت يجب فيه التحفظ على كل أدب ووقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that Yusuf was an angel followed their earlier condemnation of the Azizah and implicitly excused her: only incomparable beauty, they suggest, could overpower restraint.
rows.anchor: وكلامهن هذا بعد قولهن ذاك إعذار منهن فمفاده أن الذي كنا نقوله قبل إنما هو حق لو كان هذا بشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akbarna means they regarded him with awe; the sudden sight of overwhelming beauty eclipsed their thoughts and intentions, explaining their confused cutting, while the intensive form suggests repeated cutting.
rows.anchor: الإكبار الإعظام وهو كناية عن اندهاشهن وغيبتهن عن شعورهن وإرادتهن بمفاجأة مشاهدة ذاك الحسن الرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with “Glory be to God” before declaring Yusuf innocent follows the etiquette of first exalting God when speaking to exonerate someone; 24:16 offers a parallel.
rows.anchor: فهن لما أردن تنزيهه عليه السلام بقولهن { ما هذا بشرا } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Yusuf a noble angel reflects their belief that angels are exalted sources of goodness, beauty, knowledge, and joy, imagined in ideal human forms; the phrase praises his inner and outer qualities.
rows.anchor: وهذا بناء على ما يعتقده المليون منهم الوثنيون أن الملائكة موجودات شريفة هم مبادئ كل خير وسعادة في العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women did not initially mean to excuse the Azizah; their praise was involuntary, and she invoked their exposed actions and words only afterward to make them admit her point.
rows.anchor: وتقدم قولهن هذا على قول امرأة العزيز { فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه } يدل على أنهن لم يفهمن بهذا الكلام إعذار لامرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported interpretation identifies “that is God's favor upon us and people” as knowledge of dream interpretation, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this is far from the context.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم في معنى الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr denotes the preferable, chosen option in a comparison; Yusuf's question asks which side should be chosen for worship, not which deity exists or originated all things.
rows.anchor: { ءأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار } الخ مسوق لبيان الحجة على تعينه تعالى للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prisoners' “divided lords” include angels assigned to differentiated divine attributes or benefits, jinn associated with evil, revered humans and rulers, and the separate idols representing them.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يعبدون الملائكة وهم عندهم صفات الله سبحانه أو تعينات ذاته المقدسة التي تستند إليها جهات الخير والسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the One, the Subduer directly counters the supposed multiplicity and separation among the lords.
rows.anchor: وقابل الأرباب المتفرقين بذكر الله عز اسمه ووصفه بالواحد القهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is unbounded, eternal existence; any attribute separate from His essence would impose a limit, while every true perfection such as knowledge and power is identical with His essence.
rows.anchor: فهو تعالى ذات غير محدود ووجود غير متناه بحب، وإذا كان كذلك لم يمكن أن يفرض له صفة خارجة عن ذاته مباينة لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is one in essence and attributes: no other being exists independently, and no real divine quality is separate from Him; He alone subdues all.
rows.anchor: فهو تعالى أحدي الذات والصفات أي إنه واحد في وجوده بذاته ليس قباله شيء إلا موجودا به لا مستقلا بالوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wāḥid al-qahhār is not numerical oneness; it rules out independent beings or separable attributes, so worship cannot be divided among supposed lords or directed to an attribute apart from God.
rows.anchor: أي إنه تعالى واحد لكن لا واحد عددي إذا أضيف إليه آخر صار اثنين بل واحد لا يمكن أن يفرض قباله ذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument concludes that worship of a divine attribute apart from God would worship neither the attribute nor the essence; only the one God is a coherent object of worship.
rows.anchor: فمن عبد الذات عبد الذات والصفات ومن عبد علمه فقد عبد ذاته، وإن عبد علمه ولم يعبد ذاته فلم يعبد لا علمه ولا ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pagans may claim God is too exalted for human understanding, so they approach Him through noble creatures thought to manage the world and intercede for them; Yusuf rejects that rationale.
rows.anchor: من أن الله سبحانه أجل وأرفع ذاتا من أن تحيط به عقولنا أو يناله أفهامنا فلا يمكننا التوجه إليه بعبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf first addresses his two prison companions, then generalizes because the judgment applies to all idolaters.
rows.anchor: بدأ عليه السلام بخطاب صاحبيه في السجن أولا ثم عمم الخطاب للجميع لأن الحكم مشترك بينهما وبين غيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying they worship only names implies no realities behind the deities' labels; their names were invented by people and ancestors, with no revealed proof for them.
rows.anchor: ونفى العبادة إلا عن الأسماء كناية عن أنه لا مسميات وراء هذه الأسماء فتقع العبادة في مقابل الأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lack of divine authority concerns worship itself: God gave no proof that these beings can intercede or independently affect the world.
rows.anchor: ومن الجائز أن يكون ضمير { بها } عائدا إلى العبادة أي ما أنزل الله حجة على عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭān means an argument that can prevail over the mind; the phrase denies any such proof for the named deities.
rows.anchor: والسلطان هو البرهان لتسلطه على العقول أي ما أنزل الله بهذه الأسماء أو بهذه التسمية من برهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God truly judges because judgment requires complete control over affairs, and only He owns the world's direction and care; this supports both the absence of proof and the command to worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: إذ الحكم في أمر ما لا يستقيم إلا ممن يملك تمام التصرف، ولا مالك للتصرف والتدبير في أمور العالم وتربية العباد حقيقة إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prior commentator's wording may suggest that the dry ears number seven, but it yields only a probability, not a necessary conclusion.
rows.anchor: وكلامه على اشتماله على نكتة لطيفة لا ينتج أزيد من الظن بكون السنبلات اليابسات سبعا كغيرها أما وجوب الدلالة من الكلام فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian king asks his council to explain a dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven thin cows, alongside seven green ears and others dry.
rows.anchor: وقال ملك مصر لملئه إني أرى في منامي سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع بقرات مهازيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreams are images formed within the sleeper without sensory input; the Arabic root also yields terms for reason, maturity, and forbearance because they involve ordered thought.
rows.anchor: هو ما يراه النائم في منامه وكأن الأصل في معناه ما يتصور للإنسان من داخل نفسه من غير توصله إليه بالحس

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says the root's original sense is forbearance; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī regards that etymology as strained.
rows.anchor: وذكر الراغب إن الأصل في معناه الحلم بكسر الحاء، ولا يخلو من تكلف

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines a ḍighth as a handful of herbs, grass, or rods; “confused dreams” metaphorically describes a jumble whose parts cannot be interpreted separately.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الضغث قبضة ريحان أو حشيش أو قضبان وجمعه أضغاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite dual construct “jumbles of dreams” suggests assorted dream fragments mixed together; a sleeper may pass through several dreams, while the Qur'an does not explicitly say the king had one dream (the Torah separates them).
rows.anchor: وتسمية الرؤيا الواحدة بأضغاث الأحلام كأنه بعناية دعوى كونها صورا متفرقة مختلطة مجتمعة من رؤى مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “the dreams” is definite for this particular jumble, the counselors cannot interpret this dream; if generic, they cannot interpret every kind, though they may interpret coherent dreams, so the statements do not conflict.
rows.anchor: إن كان الألف واللام للعهد فالمعنى وما نحن بتأويل هذه المنامات التي هي أضغاث أحلام بعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to Yusuf's sending the messenger back and requesting a verdict; the two aims are to assure the Aziz of his innocence and to teach that traitors cannot ultimately achieve their schemes.
rows.anchor: فالإشارة بقوله { ذلك } إلى إرجاع الرسول إلى الملك وسؤاله القضاء، والضمير في { ليعلم } و { لم أخنه } عائد إلى العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's failure to guide traitors' schemes means falsehood cannot endure: the women's and Azizah's plots were exposed, and Yusuf's innocence prevailed.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن يعلم أن الخائن مطلقا لا ينال بخيانته غايته وأنه سيفتضح لا محالة سنة الله التي قد خلت في عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's statement shows he understands this moral law, establishing that one who did not betray a person in private can be trusted with life, honor, and property; this prepares for his request over the storehouses.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان لم يخنه في عرضه بالغيب ولا يخون في شيء البتة كان جديرا بأن يؤتمن على كل شيء نفسا كان أو عرضا أو مالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king who later summons Yusuf is not the Aziz who bought him or the husband found at the door.
rows.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في أن هذا الملك هو غير عزيز مصر زوج المرأة الذي أشير إليه بقوله { وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's “I do not absolve myself” immediately prevents his claim of innocence from sounding self-congratulatory; he attributes his goodness to mercy rather than personal power.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن قوله { أني لم أخنه بالغيب } كان لا يخلو من شائبة دعوى الحول والقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about the soul's urging evil is compared with Shuʿayb's denial of independent power or success apart from God.
rows.anchor: فقوله هذا كقول شعيب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I do not absolve myself” means Yusuf was not praising himself; human nature seeks its many desires, so only God's mercy turns it from evil and enables right action.
rows.anchor: أي إن النفس بطبعها تدعو إلى مشتهياتها من السيئات على كثرتها ووفورها فمن الجهل أن تبرأ من الميل إلى السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Except whom my Lord has mercy” both limits the claim that the soul always urges evil and shows that good deeds remain the person's own, not acts compelled by God; Yusuf's avoidance of betrayal likewise came through mercy.
rows.anchor: يفيد أن اقتراف الحسنات الذي هو برحمة من الله سبحانه من أمر النفس وليس يقع عن إلجاء وإجبار من جانبه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness covers innate deficiency and its consequences, while mercy brings forth good; divine forgiveness also addresses defects beyond sins, as in the rule for necessity.
rows.anchor: لأن المغفرة تستر النقيصة اللازمة للطبع والرحمة يظهر بها الأمر الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf calls God “my Lord” three times when speaking of personal gifts and mercy, reinforcing monotheism; he uses “Allah” for the general law that traitors' plots fail.
rows.anchor: فقد كرره ثلاثا حيث قال { إن ربي بكيدهن عليم } { إلا ما رحم ربي } { إن ربي غفور رحيم }

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators treat both verses as the Azizah's speech: her confession would let Yusuf know she had not betrayed him, God's refusal to guide traitors explains her failed plot, and she admits her own evil nature.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر جمع من المفسرين أن الآيتين أعني قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls that attribution very weak: if the Azizah speaks, “so he may know I did not betray him” makes her confession self-referential and suggests she confessed for Yusuf to hear, not to establish the truth.
rows.anchor: وهذا وجه رديء جدا أما أولا فلأن قوله { ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب } لو كان من كلام امرأة العزيز
